parsed.explanation: Strong visitor-facing protections: no criminalization, X marker on passports/IDs since 2024, anti-discrimination and transphobia-as-crime framework actively enforced (businesses fined, femicide law extended to trans women), bathroom rights affirmed, custody placement by self-declared preference with judicial consultation. Countervailing: a 2026 review still records significant violence/discrimination in practice; drink-spiking robberies and fatal dating-app robbery schemes target LGBTQ people; rising religious intolerance and threats against trans candidates. A documented divergence: one state prison system houses trans women in male units with recurring rights violations — a state-imposed exposure, but limited to one system and contingent on arrest, rare for visitors. No border friction, no universal facility ban, no organised state targeting. Subnational care-continuity issues are largely resident-facing. Protections demonstrably operate; residual exposure is street violence and imperfect implementation rather than institutional hostility.
